author: GamingBolt
description:
Whether you’re someone who is looking to re-experience Resident Evil 7 on the Nintendo Switch 2, or someone who is looking to jump into the game for the first time ever, its latest re-release on Nintendo’s current-gen platform is an excellent excuse to do just that. 

This might not be the most technically capable or polished version of the game, but it is a solid one nonetheless, and one that does nothing to dull the game’s many strengths even in the slightest. For survival horror fanatics who own a Nintendo Switch 2, Resident Evil 7 is incredibly easy to recommend.
title: Resident Evil 7: Biohazard Switch 2 Review - The Final Verdict

author: GamingBolt
description:
Sometimes, a great idea isn't enough. The gaming industry has validated that sentiment quite often over the past couple of decades, with a bunch of great game concepts never being pursued to completion thanks to internal issues, technical challenges, or simply being a victim of corporate interests interfering with creative ones. 

Whatever the case may be, it's always sad to see such promise wasting away. So, we’re presenting a few of the best ideas that should have been made into video games that may have dominated their release windows if they had ever actually been available. 

But that's not the case, and while we hold out hope that others might try to pick up on what we think were ideas ahead of their time, a fond look back at the promise they held is all we can manage for now.
title: 15 INSANE Gaming Concepts That Never Made It

author: GamingBolt
description:
With everything that was going on around the time – the outbreak in Arklay Laboratory, the operation by S.T.A.R.S., the corporate backstabbing with Wesker and Birkin – it's almost easy to forget about the non-combatants trying to live their lives. Many fell after the outbreak in Raccoon City, which only grew worse over time, but there was one who somehow managed not only to stay alive but also to escape (with some help). We're talking about none other than Sherry Birkin. 

Born in 1986, Sherry's life is pretty much what you'd expect from someone with two busy parents. Comfortable but uneventful; secure but lonely. As Dr William and Annette Birkin researched the t-Virus, and though they would be transferred to NEST, located below Raccoon City, she would rarely see them. Sherry was a student of East Raccoon Elementary, which is ironically close to the Raccoon Police Station. For her, every day was the same – wake up, go to school, come back to an empty house, and then sleep.
